Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungal infection caused by Venturia inaequalis. Spreads in wet and cool weather conditions.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Dark olive-green spots on leaves and fruits. Leaves may curl and fall early.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruits immediately.
Apply fungicide spray (Mancozeb or Captan) every 7-10 days during wet season.
Prune trees to improve air circulation.
Avoid overhead irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungal infection caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. Enters through wounds or dead wood.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown to black circular spots on fruits. Leaves show purple spots with brown centers.
treatment: Prune and destroy all dead or infected branches.
Apply copper-based fungicide during early growing season.
Remove mummified fruits from trees and ground.
Keep orchard clean of plant debris.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae requiring both apple and cedar trees.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface. Small tube-like structures on lower leaf.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Myclobutanil) from pink bud stage through summer.
Remove nearby cedar or juniper trees if possible.
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties for future planting.

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy Apple
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain good orchard hygiene.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungal disease caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis. Common in humid conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular gray to tan lesions on leaves parallel to leaf veins.
treatment: Plant resistant corn varieties.
Apply fungicide (Azoxystrobin) at early sign of infection.
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops.
Till crop residue after harvest to reduce fungal survival.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Corn Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi. Spreads through wind-blown spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small oval brick-red pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Plant rust-resistant hybrid varieties.
Apply fungicide spray if infection is severe before tasseling.
Scout fields regularly during cool and humid weather.
Early planting can help avoid peak rust season.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungal disease caused by Exserohilum turcicum. Favored by moderate temperatures and wet weather.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long elliptical gray-green to tan lesions on leaves. Can cause significant yield loss.
treatment: Plant resistant hybrid varieties.
Apply fungicide at early tasseling stage.
Rotate crops to break disease cycle.
Deep till infected crop residue after harvest.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Healthy Corn
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
treatment: Continue regular watering and fertilization.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Maintain proper spacing for air circulation.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterial infection caused by Xanthomonas vesicatoria. Spreads through rain splash and infected seeds.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow margins. Spots on fruits appear raised and scabby.
treatment: Use certified disease-free seeds.
Apply copper-based bactericide spray every 7 days.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Remove and destroy infected plant material immediately.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. Common in warm and humid conditions.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves. Yellow area surrounding spots.
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves immediately.
Apply fungicide (Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil) every 7-10 days.
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash.
Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Spreads rapidly in cool and wet conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large irregular dark brown patches on leaves. White mold visible on leaf undersides in humid weather.
treatment: Apply fungicide (Metalaxyl or Mancozeb) immediately at first sign.
Remove and destroy all infected plant parts.
Avoid wetting leaves during irrigation.
Destroy crop residue after harvest completely.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible disease symptoms.
treatment: Continue regular watering at soil level.
Apply balanced fertilizer as needed.
Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
